names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 19 iulie, «Sfântul Cuvios Die», with the rank words left off. The same site's troparion page for him spells the name «Dias».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 19 Ιουλίου, «Όσιος Δίος», with the rank word left off. The apolytikion addresses him in the vocative, «Δίε μακάριε».

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 19. јул ст. ст., „Преп. Дије.“ — «Преп.» is the rank word and is left off by §6. The form is the Serbian vernacular and not the Greek Δίος or the Romanian Die this folder already holds; the body prints the same nominative a second time, „И поживе св. Дије тачно још 15 година, и настави многе на пут спасења, многе исцели, многима поможе у разним бедама и невољама, па најзад предаде душу своју Господу, коме целога живота верно послужи.“, so nothing is restored by a reader here. `foldchk.py` returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` and `sr-foldpred.mjs` `new key, other holders: 0 (none)`. **Four characters, so it is inside duplicate detection and not under its floor.**

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 19 iulie — «Sfântul Cuvios Die»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 19ης Ιουλίου — «Όσιος Δίος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 19 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and the man is the folder's own: «Ο Όσιος Δίος καταγόταν από την Αντιόχεια της Συρίας», and in Constantinople «ίδρυσε και μοναστήρι», which is the Antioch and the monastery doxologia's life of «Sfântul Cuvios Die» tells. The Greek page adds the ordination — «τον προσκάλεσε ο Πατριάρχης Αττικός (406 - 425 μ.Χ.) στην Κωνσταντινούπολη και τον χειροτόνησε ιερέα» — and that his fame had spread by the age of thirty-five, and that he once fell ill to the point of death and was saved by a miracle. The page's two time anchors do not agree with each other: it sets him «στα χρόνια του μεγάλου Θεοδοσίου», whose reign ended in 395, and then has him ordained by Atticus, whose patriarchate it dates 406–425. Neither is a year of his own, so no `dates` are proposed and the disagreement is recorded here. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. The page prints an apolytikion and a kontakion, both of which name him, and both are taken.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 01.08.2026 (19. јул ст. ст.) — „Преп. Дије.“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, quoted whole with its closing full stop (§4). «Преп.» is the `venerable` this folder already carries; `abbot` and `wonderworker` beside it are not in the heading and are left exactly as they stand, though the body corroborates the second word for word — „Пошто издржа дуготрајну и трудну борбу са ђаволом и похоти телесном, даде му се од Бога велики дар чудотворства.“, a great gift of wonderworking given him of God. **A FIRST DATE, AND THE FIELD WAS EMPTY.** `dates` was absent from this folder altogether before today: doxologia gives no year and saint.gr dates only Atticus’s patriarchate, 406 to 425. This entry ends „Упокоји се 430. год. у дубокој старости.“ — he reposed in the year 430, in a deep old age. `death` earliest 430, latest 430, display «430», basis traditional, the sentence in the note. **An empty field is filled and no interval is displaced.** **AND THE TWO BOOKS NAME TWO DIFFERENT EMPERORS, WHICH IS RECORDED AND NOT REPAIRED.** saint.gr, already quoted in this folder’s prose, has him living «in the years of Theodosius the Great», who died in 395 and whose folder this one already relates in both directions. This book has „Слава о њему убрзо се распростре, тако да га и сам цар Теодосије Млађи посети, да прими савет од њега, а патријарх Атик приволи га те га рукоположи за презвитера.“ — the emperor Theodosius the YOUNGER himself visited him to take counsel of him, and the patriarch Atticus prevailed on him and ordained him presbyter. **Theodosius the Younger reigned 408 to 450 and this book puts the repose in 430, so the two statements of this folder are of two different reigns thirty-five years apart.** Neither is adjusted, neither is averaged and the existing `related` row to `theodosius-the-great` is left standing: a reader does not repair a source. The year written is the year this book states, and it is the book that names the later emperor. WHAT THIS BOOK ADDS. THREE WONDERS NAMED OUTRIGHT, which neither other book has: „Твораше чудеса велика и страшна силом молитве своје: тако учини те сух штап озелени, сух бунар напуни се водом, неверна човека умртви и опет васкрсе.“ — he made a dry staff grow green, he filled a dry well with water, and he put an unbelieving man to death and raised him again. „У молитвама својим најчешће се обраћаше св. Тројици.“, in his prayers he turned most often to the Holy Trinity. AND THE DEATH THAT WAS NOT ONE: „Вест о његовој смрти привуче многи народ; дође и патријарх Атик, заједно с патријархом Антиохијским Александром.“ — news of his death drew a great crowd, and the patriarch Atticus came to it together with Alexander the patriarch of Antioch, **and when they would have buried him he rose up all at once as though waking out of sleep** and said «God has granted me fifteen more years of this life»; and he lived exactly fifteen years more. The folder’s Romanian account has him told the hour of his death by a man who appeared to him and then dying once; this one has him raised at his own funeral, and the two are left side by side. TWO ROWS ADDED AND ONE REFUSED. `atticus-of-constantinople` is a folder of this corpus, patriarch of Constantinople and dated 425, and HE IS THE MAN WHO ORDAINED THIS SAINT, so he belongs to the story and takes a row both ways; the folder’s own Greek paragraph already named him unlinked and he had no row at all. `theodosius-the-younger` takes a row both ways for the same reason, the visit being an act of the entry. **ALEXANDER THE PATRIARCH OF ANTIOCH GETS NOTHING, ON RULING 3**: `ls saints | grep -i ’^alexander’` returns more than forty folders and not one of them is a patriarch of Antioch — `alexander-patriarch-of-constantinople` is a different see and a different man — so he is named in the prose without a link and without a row. No `office`: the heading gives none, and `presbyter` is an ordination the body narrates and not a rank the heading grants. No `locations`: Antioch of Syria and Constantinople are named in clauses. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.

hymns.text: Locuitor pustiului şi înger în trup şi de minuni făcător te-ai arătat, purtătorule de Dumnezeu, părintele nostru Dias; cu postul, cu privegherea, cu rugăciunea, cereşti daruri luând, vindeci pe cei bolnavi şi sufletele celor ce aleargă la tine cu credinţă. Slavă Celui Ce ţi-a dat ţie putere; slavă Celui Ce te-a încununat pe tine; Slavă Celui Ce lucrează prin tine tuturor tămăduiri.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfântului Cuvios Dias», Glasul 1 — the common of an ascetic; the page spells the name «Dias» where the day's line has «Die».

english.text: A dweller of the desert and an angel in the body and a worker of wonders you were shown to be, God-bearing father Dias; by fasting, by vigil and by prayer you received heavenly gifts, and you heal the sick and the souls of those who run to you in faith. Glory to Him who gave you strength; glory to Him who crowned you; glory to Him who works through you healings for all.

hymns.text: Ὁ βίον ἐφάμιλλον, τὴ κλήσει πολιτευθεῖς, τῆς δόξης τοῦ Πνεύματος, πυξίον ὤφθης σεπτόν, Πατὴρ ἠμῶν Ὅσιε, σὺ γὰρ θαυματουργίαις, ἱεραὶς διαπρεπῶν, ἔνδοξος ἐν Ὀσίοις, φερωνύμως ἐδείχθης. Διὸ σὲ ἀνευφημοῦμεν, Δίε μακάριε.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος δ’, Ταχὺ προκατάλαβε — the first of the two hymns on the page of «Όσιος Δίος», and it names him in its last line

english.text: Having lived a life that matched your calling, you were shown to be a venerable tablet of the Spirit's glory, our venerable father; for excelling in holy wonderworking you were shown glorious among the venerable, true to the name you bear. Therefore we sing your praise, blessed Dios.

hymns.text: Ἁγνείᾳ ψυχῆς, ἐνθέως ὁπλισάμενος, καὶ ἄπαυστον εὐχήν, ὡς λόγχην χειρισάμενος, κραταιῶς διέκοψας, τῶν δαιμόνων Δίε τὰς φάλαγγας, θαυματουργὲ Πατὴρ ἡμῶν, πρεσβεύων ἀπαύστως ὑπὲρ πάντων ἡμῶν.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος β’, Τὰ ἄνω ζητῶν — the second of the two hymns on the page of «Όσιος Δίος», and it names him

english.text: Armed by God with purity of soul, and handling unceasing prayer as a spear, you cut mightily through the phalanxes of the demons, Dios, our wonderworking father, interceding without ceasing for us all.

death.note: Охридски пролог: „Упокоји се 430. год. у дубокој старости.“
